name: Color Health
desc: Provides hereditary cancer genetic testing and cancer care programmes to employers, health systems and governments, plus some consumer tests.
markets: Customers are US employers, health systems and public bodies; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Healthcare B2B brand with a US focus; limited consumer marketing need, though employer-benefit audiences could be reached through hospitality.

name: Inventage Lab
desc: Develops sustained-release injectable drug delivery technology based on microsphere platforms, working with pharmaceutical partners on licensed products.
markets: Pharma partnerships and licensing; no verified details on international markets beyond partner deals.
rationale: B2B pharma platform with no consumer brand and little visibility beyond biotech; sponsorship value is low.

name: Wilson Wolf Corporation
desc: Makes G-Rex cell culture flasks used to grow immune cells for cell and gene therapy research and manufacturing.
markets: Sells to cell therapy developers and research labs; no verified details of international operations.
rationale: Niche laboratory supplier selling to scientists; no consumer brand, so weak F1 fit.

name: Tivic Health Systems
desc: Sells ClearUP, a handheld bioelectronic device for sinus pain and congestion relief, to consumers online and through retailers.
markets: Sold in the United States online and through retailers; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Small consumer health brand with limited budget; F1 audience reach is attractive but company is micro-cap.

name: Galapagos
desc: Belgian biotechnology company discovering and developing small-molecule medicines for inflammatory and other diseases, including filgotinib marketed as Jyseleca.
markets: Operations in Europe and the US, with filgotinib marketed in Europe and Japan through partners.
rationale: Listed biotech with no consumer brand; B2B hospitality could suit investors, but fit is weak.

name: Horizon Therapeutics
desc: Developed and sold medicines for rare, autoimmune and severe inflammatory diseases, such as Tepezza, Krystexxa and Uplizna.
markets: Medicines sold in the United States and Europe, with operations in Illinois; now part of Amgen.
rationale: Now absorbed into Amgen; no standalone brand to market, so no independent F1 case.

name: ANGUS Chemical
desc: Produces specialty nitroalkane chemicals and derivatives, such as amino alcohols and biocides, used in paints, coatings and metalworking fluids.
markets: Sells to industrial formulators; no verified detail of overseas operations.
rationale: Industrial B2B ingredient supplier with little consumer visibility; F1 hospitality could suit customers but fit is weak.

name: BGI Group
desc: Chinese genomics group selling DNA sequencers, reagents and genetic testing services through units such as MGI Tech and BGI Genomics.
markets: Sequencers and genetic tests sold in Asia, Europe and the Americas, with overseas subsidiaries.
rationale: Global genomics brand but B2B science buyers; technology showcase possible, though political sensitivity limits fit.

name: EQRx
desc: Was a biotechnology company aiming to develop and sell cancer and immunology drugs at much lower prices than existing therapies.
markets: Pre-revenue drug developer; the company merged into Revolution Medicines in 2023.
rationale: Merged out of existence with no brand to market; no F1 case.

name: Invitae
desc: Offered clinical genetic testing panels for hereditary cancer, rare disease and reproductive health before its 2024 bankruptcy.
markets: US-based genetic testing; filed for bankruptcy in 2024 with assets later bought by Labcorp.
rationale: Bankrupt business whose assets were absorbed by another company, so it has no brand to market in F1.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2024; assets acquired by Labcorp

name: Sage Therapeutics
desc: Developed neuropsychiatric medicines including Zulresso and Zurzuvae for postpartum depression, the latter co-commercialised with Biogen.
markets: Products sold in the United States; company acquired by Supernus Pharmaceuticals in 2025.
rationale: Now part of Supernus with no standalone brand; no real F1 case.

name: Seagen
desc: Developed antibody-drug conjugate cancer medicines including Adcetris and Padcev, and is now part of Pfizer.
markets: Cancer medicines sold in the US, Europe and Asia; acquired by Pfizer in 2023.
rationale: Absorbed into Pfizer, so no separate marketing budget or brand; no independent F1 case.

name: Assertio Holdings
desc: US specialty pharmaceutical company that acquires and sells branded prescription medicines for pain, neurology and inflammatory conditions.
markets: Prescription products sold in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic prescription brands with strict promotion rules and limited consumer marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: IVERIC bio
desc: Developed Izervay for geographic atrophy, an advanced eye disease, and was acquired by Astellas in 2023.
markets: Izervay approved in the United States in 2023; company acquired by Astellas.
rationale: Absorbed into Astellas, so it has no independent brand or marketing budget; no standalone F1 case.

name: Taibang Biological Group
desc: Chinese plasma products group collecting human plasma and producing albumin, immunoglobulins and clotting factors.
markets: Plasma products sold in China; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic plasma producer with no consumer marketing culture and limited international presence; weak F1 fit.

name: ViewRay
desc: Made the MRIdian MRI-guided radiation therapy system for hospitals and cancer centres before filing for bankruptcy in 2023.
markets: Sold MRIdian systems to hospitals in the US, Europe and Asia; filed for bankruptcy in 2023.
rationale: Bankrupt hospital equipment maker with no brand to market; no F1 case.

name: CymaBay Therapeutics
desc: Developed seladelpar for primary biliary cholangitis and other liver diseases, and was acquired by Gilead Sciences in 2024.
markets: Drug development in the United States; acquired by Gilead in 2024.
rationale: Absorbed into Gilead with no stand-alone brand or marketing budget; no independent F1 case.

name: IGM Biosciences
desc: Developed engineered IgM antibodies for cancer and autoimmune disease, with imvotamab as lead candidate, before scaling back operations.
markets: Pre-revenue clinical-stage developer in the United States; restructured around 2025.

name: MorphoSys
desc: German antibody biotech known for Monjuvi for lymphoma, marketed with Incyte, and acquired by Novartis in 2024.
markets: Monjuvi marketed in the United States and Europe; acquired by Novartis in 2024.
rationale: Absorbed into Novartis with no stand-alone brand or marketing budget; no independent F1 case.

name: Pliant Therapeutics
desc: Clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for fibrotic diseases, with bexotegrast as its lead candidate.
markets: Pre-revenue drug developer running clinical trials; no commercial sales.
rationale: Pre-revenue drug developer with no consumer brand to market; very weak F1 fit.

name: Shockwave Medical
desc: Makes intravascular lithotripsy catheter systems that break up calcified plaque in arteries, now owned by Johnson & Johnson.
markets: Devices sold in the US, Europe and Asia; acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2024.
rationale: Now inside Johnson & Johnson MedTech; no separate marketing case for F1.

name: Arcellx
desc: Clinical-stage biotechnology company developing CAR-T cell therapies for cancer, with anito-cel developed together with Kite, a Gilead company.

name: Nimbus Therapeutics

name: RefleXion Medical
desc: Makes the X1 radiotherapy system, combining a linear accelerator with PET imaging, sold to hospitals and cancer centres.

name: Syros Pharmaceuticals
desc: Developed gene-control cancer medicines such as tamibarotene for blood cancers, but never had an approved product.
markets: Pre-revenue developer in the United States; tamibarotene failed in 2024 and the company wound down.

name: Adaptimmune
desc: Develops engineered T cell receptor therapies for solid tumours, including FDA-approved Tecelra for synovial sarcoma.
markets: Operations in the UK and United States; sold commercial assets to US WorldMeds in 2025.

name: BioNexus Gene Lab

name: NGM Biopharmaceuticals

name: Opthea

name: Ventyx Biosciences
desc: Develops oral NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors and other small molecules for inflammatory diseases, such as obesity-related inflammation and Parkinson's disease.

name: Molecular Templates

name: Torrent Pharmaceuticals
desc: Indian drugmaker in the Torrent Group focused on chronic cardiovascular, central nervous system, gastroenterology and diabetes medicines.

name: TScan Therapeutics
desc: Develops T cell receptor engineered T cell therapies aimed at preventing relapse in blood cancers such as acute myeloid leukaemia.
markets: Pre-revenue developer in the United States with no commercial sales.
rationale: Pre-revenue drug developer with no consumer brand to market; weak F1 fit.

name: Capricor Therapeutics

name: Corbus Pharmaceuticals

name: Exagen

name: METiS Pharmaceuticals
